items.text: Business Standard confirmed: Brent crude rose 3.01% to $114.60/barrel — highest since April 7. WTI surged 4.94% to $101.10 earlier in session. The Week: "Brent crude was trading around $111 per barrel Wednesday morning." CBS News: "Brent Crude topped $112 a barrel Tuesday with no clear indication of an imminent resolution." items.bold: UAE LEAVING OPEC + OPEC+ EFFECTIVE MAY 1 — historic 6-decade shift. India implications.
items.text: The Week (updated 10:51 IST April 29) confirmed: UAE announced it is leaving both OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, 2026 — "a shock decision in the country's national interest following a comprehensive review of its production policy and capacity." UAE had been secretly exceeding OPEC quotas. The Week: for India, "the development is the most consequential energy market shift in years." Post-departure, UAE is "widely expected to ramp output toward its stated ambition of 5 million barrels per day by 2027." UAE's exit from OPEC + strong bilateral ties with India = better supply terms and pricing for Indian refiners in the medium term. "OPEC's share of India's crude imports had already slipped below 50% in FY2025, its lowest ever." Brent barely moved on the UAE news — "since the market's dominant driver remains the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz." UAE exit helps India structurally but not in the immediate crisis.

military.t: QATAR Warned of "FROZEN CONFLICT" — Most Significant Gulf State Signal of the War.
military.d: CBS News (live blog) confirmed: Qatar warned of the possibility of a "frozen conflict" in the Gulf as talks between the US and Iran appeared to be at a stalemate. Qatar is the single most important Gulf state signal in this war — it hosts the largest US military air base in the Middle East (Al Udeid) AND the Ras Laffan LNG terminal (partially damaged, QatarEnergy force majeure). Qatar's "frozen conflict" warning is not casual diplomatic language — it means Qatar's leadership believes the war could become indefinitely prolonged with no clear resolution, similar to the Korea or Israel-Palestine conflicts. For India: Qatar = 60% of India's natural gas. Ras Laffan 17% capacity damaged. A "frozen conflict" means the Ras Laffan supply disruption becomes structural, not temporary. India must accelerate diversification of gas supply.

assessment.body:
Wednesday 7 PM IST. Day 61. Markets recovered. Oil surged. Qatar warned the world.

THE MARKET RECOVERY
• Sensex +609 to 77,496. Nifty +182 to 24,178. VIX -3% to 17.4
• Three-day losing streak ended on bargain buying and strong Q4 earnings
• ITC +3.79%, Tech Mahindra +3.31%, Reliance +3.22% top gainers
• FMCG and Realty outperformed — defensive growth plays
• Broader markets: MidCap -0.07%, SmallCap +0.65%
• Markets shrugged off Brent at $114 on earnings optimism
• But VIX at 17.4 still elevated vs pre-war 12-14

THE OIL SHOCK
• Brent +3.01% to $114.60 — highest since April 7
• WTI surged 4.94% to $101.10
• UAE OPEC exit barely moved markets — Hormuz is the driver, not quotas
• IEA: greatest global energy security challenge in history

THE QATAR WARNING — MOST IMPORTANT SIGNAL OF THE DAY
• Qatar warned of "frozen conflict" in the Gulf
• Qatar = US Al Udeid Air Base + Ras Laffan LNG (60% of India's gas)
• "Frozen conflict" = indefinitely prolonged war without resolution
• Like Korea or Israel-Palestine — decades of stalemate
• For India: structural LNG supply disruption, not temporary
• India must urgently diversify gas imports

THE DIPLOMATIC STALEMATE
• WH counterproposal to Iran still not delivered
• Rubio rejected Iran's decoupled Hormuz-first proposal
• Trump: Iran in "State of Collapse"
• Iran: official position "Hormuz remains closed" (Tehran billboard)
• Operational reality: Idemitsu Maru passed with Iran coordination
• Selective Hormuz control emerging — not blanket closure

INDIA'S POSITION AT 7 PM
• Sensex 77,496 — recovered from 76,887 lows
• VIX 17.4 — easing but not pre-war levels
• Brent $114.60 = OMC hike Rs 5-9/L Thursday-Friday
• Qatar frozen conflict = structural India LNG risk
• UAE OPEC exit = medium-term positive for India crude supply
• Fed rate decision tonight — will drive rupee and FII direction
• India IP 4.1% March — war impact on manufacturing confirmed

VERDICT: Wednesday brought a Sensex recovery and a Qatar warning that may be the most strategically significant signal of the war. Markets can rally on earnings. They cannot rally on a frozen conflict that permanently disrupts India's energy supply chains. The WH counterproposal — when it comes — will determine whether the war ends or freezes.
